KIT styles and browser-side scripts (an htmltools dependency)

Source: R/setup.R
use_kit.Rd

Can go anywhere in the page (htmltools moves it into <head>). It contains:

Usage

use_kit()

Value

An htmltools::htmlDependency() object.

Details

  • kit-base.css: basic styles for the header, guide boxes, callouts, and so on (formerly kit_css(), kit_css_guide()).

  • kit-brite.css: KIT's neo-brutalism styles (formerly kit_css_brite()).

  • kit-design.css: the few rules kitDesign adds (header layout, dashed tabs in flow tabs, code box width).

  • kit.js: collapsible sections, tab bars, tab states, scrolling to results, the reminder before leaving, and the "複製" ("Copy") button.

kit_page() already adds it; you only need to add use_kit() when you build the page yourself with bslib::page_*(), and pass theme = kit_theme() to the page.

Examples

use_kit()
#> List of 10
#>  $ name      : chr "kitDesign"
#>  $ version   : chr "0.6.1"
#>  $ src       :List of 1
#>   ..$ file: chr "www"
#>  $ meta      : NULL
#>  $ script    : chr "kit.js"
#>  $ stylesheet: chr [1:3] "kit-base.css" "kit-brite.css" "kit-design.css"
#>  $ head      : NULL
#>  $ attachment: NULL
#>  $ package   : chr "kitDesign"
#>  $ all_files : logi FALSE
#>  - attr(*, "class")= chr "html_dependency"
